compilers.name: Visual C++ 6 SP6
compilers.note: The only compiler that is CRC-compatible with retail Generals 1.08 / Zero Hour 1.04.

compilers.name: Modern MSVC (VS2022)
compilers.note: A modern compiler: easier to debug.

compilers.name: MinGW-w64 + Clang (container)
compilers.note: Open-source cross compiler (clang 18). Its whole build environment ships as a container image (Docker or Podman) or runs in WSL, so it works on any computer, Windows or not. The Profile build leaves out function-level call tracing, which the game source writes in MSVC-only assembly.

compilers.name: MinGW-w64 + GCC (container)
compilers.note: Open-source cross compiler (gcc), in the same kind of container image. There is no Profile build: the game's profiling code is MSVC-only assembly that gcc cannot compile.

compilers.name: Linux (native)
compilers.note: Builds natively on a Linux computer, using the build agent for Linux. It does not run in a container or on another operating system.

compilers.name: macOS (Apple silicon, native)
compilers.note: Builds natively on a Mac with Apple silicon, using the build agent for macOS. It does not run in a container or on another operating system.

groups.name: Retail bugs and quirks

switches.title: Deterministic math
switches.why: Visual C++ 6 uses its own x87 assembly, so deterministic math does not apply.
switches.help: Use fdlibm-based deterministic math, for replay validation across platforms.

switches.title: ccache
switches.help: Use the ccache compiler cache when it is installed.

switches.title: In-game update check
switches.help: Check GitHub Releases for a newer version from inside the game. Auto: on when SDL3 is on.

switches.title: GLM math library
switches.help: Use the GLM math library as the DirectX 8 replacement. Auto: as the preset has it.

switches.title: Direct3D 8 renderer
switches.help: Use the real Direct3D 8 renderer, or DXVK. Auto: as the preset has it.

switches.title: Render backend
switches.why: Visual C++ 6 can only use the DirectX 8 backend.
switches.help: Rendering backend for the graphics engine. bgfx is cross-platform (DirectX 11, Vulkan or Metal) and needs a modern compiler.

switches.title: bgfx renderer
switches.why: Only used with the bgfx render backend.
switches.help: Which graphics API bgfx drives (the Linux presets use Vulkan, the macOS presets Metal).

switches.title: Diagnostic runtime flags

switches.title: Preserve retail behaviour

rules.message: Stack tracing implies debug logging, so logging cannot be OFF.
ASAN needs the game memory allocator off (it overrides new/delete).
The weekly config is VC6 only.

tier2.name: Retail fixes enabled
tier2.blurb: Retail compatibility OFF: gameplay and network fixes that break retail CRC.

tier2.name: Retail forced on
tier2.blurb: Retail compatibility ON explicitly (what the source does anyway, kept as a reference build).

tier2.name: No game memory allocator
tier2.blurb: Uses the CRT heap; handy for third-party memory tools.

tier2.name: Memory pool paranoia
tier2.blurb: Every memory pool checker on. Very slow; for hunting corruption.

tier2.name: Release with full diagnostics
tier2.blurb: Logging, crash dialogs, stack traces and profiling in a release build.

tier2.name: Cheats enabled
tier2.blurb: Debug cheats in a release build. Single player only.

tier2.name: Multi-instance
tier2.blurb: Run several clients on one machine for network testing.

tier2.name: Address Sanitizer
tier2.blurb: Debug build with ASAN. Game memory allocator is turned off.

tier2.name: Tracy profiler
tier2.blurb: Profile build wired to the Tracy profiler.

tier2.name: Every retail bug kept
tier2.blurb: All retail bug switches ON: the original behaviour, quirks included.

tier2.name: Every retail bug fixed
tier2.blurb: All retail bug switches OFF: the fixed behaviour. Will not stay in sync with retail players.
